name: Alexander the Great
text: Alexander the Great, the Macedonian king Alexander III, lived from 356 to 323 BC. Celtic envoys from the Adriatic met him and won his audience. Asked what they feared most, they said they feared nothing but the sky falling. They prized his friendship above every danger. His link to the Celts runs through coinage. His gold and his father Philip II of Macedon's modeled the later Celtic money of Europe and Britain. The Welsh poets of the Book of Taliesin and the court poet Cynddelw cast him as a martial paragon.

attributes.attribute: welcomed Celtic envoys from the Adriatic
his father, whose coinage the Celts copied

okr.objective: Set down the meeting of Alexander and the Adriatic Celts and his fame in Celtic literature.
key_results: Alexander, king of Macedonia, received the Celtic envoys from the Adriatic.
He asked the envoys what they feared; they answered the sky falling.
The Book of Taliesin poets and Cynddelw honour him as a martial paragon.
